title: High-voltage battery module cell voltage too low
description: The battery management system measured cell voltages below the permitted minimum. The vehicle may restrict output and range until the pack is serviced.
symptoms: High-voltage battery warning in the cluster
possibleFixes: Read the cell voltage spread in the battery management system
Check for a single weak module before replacing the pack
Have the high-voltage battery inspected by a qualified workshop
definitionSource: VoltLink curation of public Mercedes-Benz service bulletins

title: High-voltage battery module cell voltage too high
description: The battery management system measured cell voltages above the permitted maximum, usually during charging or recuperation.
symptoms: High-voltage battery warning in the cluster
possibleFixes: Read the cell voltage spread while charging
Check the charge target and balancing history
Have the high-voltage battery inspected by a qualified workshop
definitionSource: VoltLink curation of public Mercedes-Benz service bulletins

title: High-voltage battery cell voltage low
description: One or more cells were measured at a voltage low enough to risk damaging the pack. Discharge is inhibited until the fault is resolved.
symptoms: Vehicle will not start or drive
Pack refuses to accept or deliver power
possibleFixes: Do not attempt to jump-start the high-voltage system
Read individual cell voltages
Arrange high-voltage battery service
definitionSource: VoltLink curation of public Mercedes-Benz service bulletins

title: High-voltage isolation fault
description: The isolation resistance between the high-voltage system and the vehicle chassis fell below the safety threshold, often after moisture or damage.
possibleFixes: Stop using the vehicle and have it recovered
Check high-voltage connectors and cable insulation
Have the isolation fault measured by a qualified workshop
definitionSource: VoltLink curation of public Mercedes-Benz service bulletins

title: High-voltage contactor did not switch as expected
description: The powertrain control unit reported that a high-voltage contactor did not reach the requested state. The car may refuse to start or to charge.
symptoms: Vehicle will not start after charging
Contactor noise without the system engaging
possibleFixes: Read the contactor states in the powertrain control unit
Check the 12V supply to the high-voltage control units
Have the contactor diagnosis performed by a qualified workshop
definitionSource: VoltLink curation of public Mercedes-Benz service bulletins

title: Overcurrent in the high-voltage charging circuit
description: The charging path reported current above the permitted limit, so charging was interrupted as a protective measure.
symptoms: Charging stops shortly after it starts
Charging warning in the cluster or app
Repeated session aborts at the same point
possibleFixes: Try a different AC charging station and cable
Read the charge current limit in the charger control unit
Have the on-board charger checked if the fault follows the car
definitionSource: VoltLink curation of public Mercedes-Benz service bulletins

title: DC charge connector contactor stuck closed
description: The direct-current charge connection unit reported that a contactor remained closed. The high-voltage system cannot be safely isolated in that state.
symptoms: High-voltage warning after a fast-charge session
possibleFixes: Do not attempt further DC charging
Read the contactor states in the DC charge connection unit
Arrange service before driving long distances
definitionSource: VoltLink curation of public Mercedes-Benz service bulletins
